item.title: A rare 1800s Washington folk art drawing, hidden for 60 years, sold at auction for $226,600
item.description: A remarkable early 19th-century folk art piece, showcasing George Washington, has achieved a staggering auction price of $226,600 after lying dormant for 60 years. This striking artwork embodies the fraktur tradition of Pennsylvania German heritage, adorned with patriotic imagery. The strong interest stemmed from its superb condition and rich historical context, illustrating the enduring passion for distinguished American folk art among collectors and institutions alike.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lauren Conrad bought a $1.35M Beverly Hills penthouse, rebuilt it, sold it for $2.8M
item.description: Lauren Conrad, known for The Hills, sold her renovated Beverly Hills penthouse for $2.8 million. She initially purchased the property for $1.35 million four years earlier. After extensive renovations, she transformed the space into a modern home with high-end finishes. The penthouse includes a large open-plan living area, multiple bedrooms, and outdoor terraces. Conrad's real estate ventures in Southern California continue to show significant financial returns.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man spent over 20 years restoring Spitfire aircraft in UK garage; project sells for £18,000
item.description: Peter Arnold, affectionately dubbed 'Mr Spitfire', dedicated over half a century to amassing historic aircraft relics. After his passing in 2025, a remarkable unfinished Spitfire fuselage went under the hammer for £18,000. This Spitfire F Mk 22 PK519 fuselage featured original components, resting in Arnold's garage for 20 years. Besides the fuselage, auctioned treasures included vintage aircraft instruments and a mesmerizing clock.

New York family blocks road with tree trunks, court awards it to neighbouring club
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a New York family has lost their claim to a shared private road that now belongs to a nearby recreational club. This road, previously amicably used for decades, became contentious in 2021 when disagreements over access arose. The state’s highest court ultimately sided with the club, citing its historical maintenance and usage, despite the family's assertions of permission based on their long-term relationship.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: DiCaprio-linked group buys 52,000 acres on Chilean island; protected status still under negotiation
item.description: In 2025, Guafo Island in Chile was acquired with a mission: to safeguard its rich wildlife and thwart harmful development. Collaborative efforts between local partners and authorities are vital in securing legal protections for the island. Engaging indigenous communities in resource negotiations enhances respect for local customs while ensuring a strategic management plan, pivotal for the island's ecological integrity and cultural preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mississippi turns 31-ton propane tank once used for firefighter training into artificial reef
item.description: A 31-ton propane tank and steel tower once used for firefighter training in Mississippi have been sunk about 13 miles offshore to create an artificial reef for marine life. Supported by Chevron and local organisations, the project aims to provide shelter for fish and improve fishing opportunities. A similar reef created in 2023 now supports more than 530 red snapper, according to official estimates.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New York couple's $6.83 million divorce award upheld after appeals court reviews business interests and payments
item.description: In a recent high-profile divorce case, Shirley F. Atkins emerged victorious with a settlement of $6.83 million from James C. Atkins. The appeals court affirmed her entitlement to 22.5% of his business interests and stock sale proceeds. Both sides presented compelling arguments to adjust this percentage. Furthermore, the court ruled on tax responsibilities and payment structures, illustrating its power in equitable asset distribution during divorce proceedings.

item.title: Canadian conservation club with just 4 members to donate nearly 100-acre forest to university for honeybee research
item.description: A conservation club plans to transfer nearly 100 acres of land on Thorah Island to the University of Guelph. This site has been dedicated to honeybee breeding research for over thirty years. The donation aims to maintain the land for conservation and research instead of development. The University of Guelph will continue its long-term apiary operation critical to honeybee genetics work.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Winston Churchill’s 1948 painting sells for £716,800; proceeds to fund arts programme
item.description: Winston Churchill's artwork, Amaryllis Lily, fetched an impressive £716,800 at auction, with proceeds directed toward the Churchill Fellowship. This funding will bolster the Making Space for the Arts initiative, aimed at increasing public participation in the arts. The piece, which has a fascinating legacy, was originally given to Churchill's daughter before being donated. This auction not only exceeded expectations but also empowers the charity to support significant artistic community initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indiana homeowner damages shared garden, calls it maintenance; appeals court upholds HOA injunction
item.description: In a legal showdown, Indiana resident Martin L. Booth clashed with the Efroymson House Owner's Association over alleged vandalism of shared garden spaces, including shrubs, flowers, and lighting. The Indiana Court of Appeals upheld an injunction against Booth, highlighting the HOA's ownership of common areas. Despite Booth's claim of property rights, the court affirmed evidence of his destructive actions, siding with the HOA.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hebron Lockdown Ordered: Netanyahu plans full West Bank closure; attack heightens election fears
item.description: In response to a recent shooting near Hebron, Israel has enacted a total closure of the occupied West Bank, citing rising security concerns as the Israeli elections approach. The alleged gunmen were reportedly neutralized, and authorities have put up roadblocks, imposing strict limitations on Palestinian movement. This has sparked vigorous discussions around security protocols and the implications for Palestinian civilians.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Florida mother seeks child support from ex, court adds new husband's $8,600 bills to her income
item.description: A Florida appeals court has determined that child support calculations will be revisited in a contentious family dispute. Bianca Rampartap sought a review after her ex-husband halted his parenting time. The earlier court wrongly counted his financial contributions as income for Bianca, leading her to appeal. The higher court ruled in her favor, requiring a reexamination of her income and subsequent modifications to child support arrangements.

item.title: South Korean rescuers try three times to free shark, but it swims back into canal
item.description: A dusky shark, named Bukangi, has remained in the North Port canal in Busan for over a month. Authorities have attempted multiple rescues, but the shark keeps returning to the canal. Experts believe busy port activities may be influencing Bukangi's behavior, making it feel safer in the canal. The shark, which is endangered, has raised concerns due to lack of feeding and falling water temperatures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Old deeds and a 1926 ruling shaped Florida rail land dispute as court rejects trail compensation claims
item.description: In a recent ruling, the US Court of Appeals clarified property rights as Florida landowners sought compensation when a railway corridor transformed into a public trail. The court determined that the railway held fee simple ownership of the land, supported by historical deeds and a condemnation judgment, nullifying any reversionary rights for landowners. Ultimately, this ruling emphasizes the significance of historical property rights in present-day legal scenarios.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
